Q: PIL - Images not rotating A:

From the docs:

Image.rotate(angle, resample=0, expand=0, center=None, translate=None)

Returns a rotated copy of this image. This method returns a copy of this image, rotated the given number of degrees counter clockwise around its centre.

The image is not rotated in place. You need to store the image returned from rotate(). Maybe something like:

if exif_data['Orientation'] == 6:
    new_image = img.rotate(180)

Q: Why is my bot not able to detect when a user leaves in Telegram? A:

While I’m not entirely sure this’ll work, try using the my_chat_member update type instead of just chat_member. The former is specifically for updates related to the bot itself and may capture more reliable events.

Simply modify your handler:

app.add_handler(ChatMemberHandler(check_status, ChatMemberHandler.MY_CHAT_MEMBER))

Q: How to skip binary file types when cloning a Perforce repository with git-p4 A:

Create or modify a Perforce client specification (p4 client) to use exclusion mappings.

p4 client my_git_client

In the View: section of the client spec, add exclusion lines like this:

//depot/project/.... //my_client/project/....
-//depot/project/binaries/.... //my_client/project/binaries/....
-//depot/project/large_files/*.iso //my_client/project/large_files/*.iso

Use the --use-client-spec option during the git p4 clone command, specifying the name of your client.

git p4 clone --use-client-spec //depot/project/@all my_git_repo

Q: Do I still need a mac to develop react-native applications for iOS? A:

You can run a React Native app on iPhone without a Mac using Expo if it’s all JavaScript, because Expo Go interprets JS code on the device (Expo Docs ).
However, to add native iOS libraries or build the app for the App Store, you must use a Mac with Xcode and CocoaPods, because iOS apps require Xcode to compile native code (React Native Docs, CocoaPods).

Q: Importing variable from python file, which is assigned by a function A:

Each time you run from file import variable all code inside file is being executed. For all deterministic programs it would behave as you intend, but as random.random() is non-deterministic it will produce different output each time, making a variable different across every import.

A way to overcome non-deterministic behavior is to use a seed. You can write your generate.py file as:

import random

random.seed(10)
a = random.random()

You can use any integer as random.seed() method parameter. Seed will ensure that pseudo-random number generator is initialized the same way and produces the same output across every import (even if code gets more complicated and there are multiple random calls).

Q: Kibana visualization for grouping and filter A:

I believe you are looking for filterAggregation : Filter Aggregation Effectively it enables aggregation on different filters.

Add this as a second aggregation(split slice) after the Persons Aggregation.

If you are just interested in count and Not counts per person, just leverage Filter Aggregation with respective filters which will give you the percentages per filter.
